subject: HelioHealth eval pilot — readiness checklist, model recommendations & scoring guidance
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <m.patel@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: HelioHealth eval pilot — readiness checklist, model recommendations & scoring guidance

Hi Maya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps to get your pilot (clinical triage assistant) running on Redwood: 

What we captured on the call
- Goal: ~90% acceptable triage suggestions, low false-negative on urgent flags, sub-200ms median token latency target for interactive QA flows.
- Data: 20k anonymized encounter snippets + 2k annotated gold responses for initial scoring.
- Constraint: PHI-needs to stay in your VPC (you flagged audit/KMS requirements).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) You: share the first 2k labeled records in the format in the attached CSV (helio_eval_schema_v1.csv) — ideally S3 with Redshift/Glue friendly layout. (ETA: Wed EOD your time)
2) Us (Redwood): provision a Private eval run in your VPC, run baseline models, and return a scorecard + small qualitative sample. (ETA: 2 business days after data transfer)
3) Joint: 30-min review to align on scoring thresholds & human review cadence. (Propose Thu 10:00am PT)

Model recommendations (starter slate)
- Production-low-latency candidate: Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16, int8 option) — good for throughput and cheaper per-token.
- Quality-first candidate: Llama2-13B-chat (FP16) — better instruction-following and clinical nuance.
- High-capacity check (spot-check only): Llama2-70B-chat (quantized for inference) — use for identifying worst-case errors.
Notes: our Redwood Optimize module will suggest quantization/profile per workload; for the pilot we recommend starting with the 7B and 13B pair for cost/coverage. See redwood_model_recs.pdf attached for latency/cost lift estimates.

Eval runner & scoring highlights
- We run the Redwood eval harness against your reference set; default metrics we compute: exact-match (for categorical triage labels), macro F1, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine + threshold for free-text suggestions), and Top-K recall for intent picks.
- We also surface per-prompt token-latency and tail-percentile latency (p95/p99).
- Regression guardrail: we compute embedding-based similarity vs. your gold labels and flag any model where mean similarity drops > 5% vs baseline.

Compliance note
- For VPC/private runs we can accept S3 with SSE-KMS; we will provide temporary IAM role instructions and KMS key ARN to use on upload. If you need on-prem air-gapped, we can schedule an appliance review (longer lead time).

Attachments to review: helio_eval_schema_v1.csv (required format), redwood_model_recs.pdf (starter slate + cost), benchmark-instructions.md (how we run the harness).

If that looks good I’ll open the pilot ticket and drop a dedicated Drive folder with the runner scripts.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

Subject: Re: HelioHealth eval pilot — readiness checklist, model recommendations & scoring guidance

Thanks Jasmine — the recap is helpful. A couple clarifications before we upload: 

- We can put the labeled 2k set into S3 (s3://helio-prod/eval/2027-04/pilot/) with SSE-KMS and will create an upload role if you send the role ARN.
- For PHI handling: we need confirmation that the eval run will not persist token-level logs outside our VPC and that KMS encryption is enforced for any temporary artifacts.
- Scoring: our clinical QA lead wants a custom FNR (false negative rate) target for urgent flags — can you add a FNR line-item to the scorecard? We consider any FNR > 3% as a blocker.

Attached: small sample export (first_100_records_sample.jsonl) — schema looks similar to your CSV but with a few extra metadata fields. Let me know if you want that as the canonical schema.

We’re aiming to get the sample uploaded by end of day.

— Maya

m.patel@heliohealth.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <m.patel@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth eval pilot — readiness checklist, model recommendations & scoring guidance

Maya — great, thanks for the quick turn. Quick answers and next actions: 

1) S3 & KMS: we will NOT persist token-level logs outside your VPC. For Private evals the runner is deployed into your subnet and temporary artifacts are written to your S3 with the KMS key you provide. Please send the IAM role ARN and KMS ARN to secure@redwood.ai; we’ll use that for the test runs.

2) FNR metric: yes — we’ll add a dedicated false-negative-rate row to the scorecard for the urgent_flag label. Our default scorecard template now includes FNR along with precision/recall/F1. We’ll mark FNR > 3% as a blocker per your ask.

3) Canonical dataset format: we accept JSONL or CSV. Preferred JSONL record (one per line):
- id: unique string
- prompt: patient encounter text (anonymized)
- reference: gold triage label or canonical response (string)
- meta: comma-separated clinical tags (onset,duration,meds) — optional
Example line: {"id":"hh-0001", "prompt":"58yo female with chest pain...", "reference":"urgent", "meta":"cardio, ER"}

4) Scoring details we will compute (and include on the sheet):
- Categorical labels: confusion matrix, accuracy, macro F1, FNR (urgent_flag)
- Free-text suggestions: embedding-similarity (OpenAI/Redwood embeddings internally) + human spot-check: 200-sample human pass/fail
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token times + end-to-end median latency (cold vs warm cache)
- Regression alert: any metric falling >5% relative to our baseline model triggers a regression review.

5) Running the Redwood eval harness (short example)
- CLI: redwood eval run --input s3://helio-prod/eval/2027-04/pilot/first_2k.jsonl --models mistral-7b,llama2-13b --output s3://helio-prod/eval-results/HL-3421/ --scorecard-template helio_eval_schema_v1.csv
- We will provide the exact runner script in the Drive folder once the IAM role is confirmed.

6) Timeframe: once we have the 2k and role/KMS info we’ll run the baseline sweep (7B + 13B) and return a scorecard within 48 hours.

Proposed sync: Thu 10:00am PT to review thresholding and go/no-go rules — will you confirm?

— Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
